ti: Strip-mine the per-element odometer out of the reduce and broadcast VJPs
Accumulate gradients in place at fan-in, behind an explicit ownership set

note:
SITE A LANDED, SITE B NOT. Measured on M2 Pro darwin/arm64 go1.26.5, 3 reps of -benchtime 300ms, medians: BenchmarkReduceVJPSum 542,915 -> 148,228 ns (3.66x) with BenchmarkReshapeVJPFastF32 as an untouched calibration at +1.9%. The task predicted 4-6x (560 -> 95-140 us); actual 3.66x, just outside the band. ReduceVJPMean shares the code path and measures ~155 us after, but its before was never measured in this session so no ratio is claimed for it.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST: THE PATH WAS COMPLETELY UNGATED. Mutation-probing the existing suite BEFORE writing any test showed that breaking the strided gather (gs[of+j*s] -> gs[of]) and disabling the outer odometer entirely BOTH left every autograd test green — nothing exercised a non-zero innermost stride or a multi-row odometer through this VJP. A rewrite of an ungated hot loop is exactly where a silent numerical regression lands. The new cross-reference gate holds the strip-mine bit-identical to a frozen copy of the per-element loop across ranks 1-4 and every subset of reduced axes, F64 and F32, and all three mutations now turn it red. A second test pins the fallback contract: a declined shape must return false and leave the destination untouched, because returning true after writing nothing would silently zero every gradient.

NO NEW PERFSCAN RULE WAS MINTED. PS4005 per-element-odometer already flags these exact sites (vjp.go:111, vjp_reduce.go:113/:130) — it was created for this shape in an earlier round, so it is reused rather than duplicated (PROC-014). Its MESSAGE was corrected, though: it claimed bit-identity by construction flat out, which holds only for a STORING loop. For an ACCUMULATING loop the per-destination summation order must be preserved AND a hoisted scalar accumulator must keep the element type — widening to float64 and narrowing once is MORE accurate, hence a different answer. That is precisely what site B turns on, and the rule now says so.

SITE B NOT DONE: bcastSumInto (autograd/vjp.go:111), reached from the OpAdd, OpSub and OpMul VJPs — every bias gradient in every linear layer, so broader reach than site A. It is the accumulating variant, so the element-type constraint above is load-bearing, and it will need its own ungated-path probe first: assume nothing about existing coverage given what site A revealed. BenchmarkBcastReduceBiasF32 drifted 262 -> 279 us across this session while the calibration moved 1.9%; that code is untouched, so the movement is machine drift, and site B needs a fresh before/after taken in one session.

The two retained fallback odometers carry //perfscan:ignore directives, verified effective by re-running the scan (PERF-SUPPRESS-INERT-001). PS4005 tree-wide 6 -> 4.

Six autograd VJP files have NO tolerance-0 gate — build the oracle before optimizing them
MoE VJP division hoist measured and REJECTED: the loop is not divide-bound

note: No action: measured and rejected. The hoist is bit-identical and removes 8.39M divisions, and it moved the benchmark by nothing (5.51 to 5.60 ms, 6 samples per arm at 100x) because the loop gathers across e separate slices and is memory-bound. Recorded as the lesson: an operation count predicts loop cost only when the operands are resident. Retry only if the expert outputs are ever made contiguous per token.

body:
Research proposed hoisting the per-(token,expert) renormalization quotient out of the d loop in the MoE combine VJP (vjp_moe.go, both dtype arms). The argument was arithmetic and sounded strong: at the fixture (tks=4096, e=8, d=256) the mix loop performs tks*d*e = 8.39M f64 divisions, the M2 Pro FP divider is not pipelined at roughly 7 cycles throughput, and the sibling loop with the same trip count carries no division. Estimated 25 to 50 percent.

IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED: no win. BenchmarkMoECombineBackward at -benchtime=100x, 6 samples per arm: before median 5.51 ms, after median 5.60 ms. A first round at 20x was too noisy to read at all (spread over 20 percent within one arm), which is itself worth remembering for this benchmark. Reverted.

Why the estimate was wrong: the inner loop gathers es[i][eb+j] across e SEPARATE slices, so each iteration touches a different cache line and the loop is memory-bound, not divide-bound. The divider latency hides behind the loads. Counting arithmetic operations predicts the cost of a loop only when the operands are already resident.

The transform itself is sound and bit-identical (same quotient, same operands, same ascending-i accumulation) — it is simply not worth anything here. If the gather were ever restructured so the expert outputs were contiguous per token, the division would become visible again and this is the first thing to retry.

The companion suggestion from the same research, interchanging to i-outer/j-inner so the e slice headers load once per expert, was not measured separately and remains open.
